conventions.landmarkAge: age REACHED by building the landmark (Feudal = the Dark Age age-up choice). The fandom Vikings page already uses this convention; the official page confirms Valdemar Castle = Castle Age and Kongens Dør Cathedral = Imperial Age.
conventions.confidence: official = ageofempires.com / Steam store text; wiki = ageofempires.fandom.com (pages created 2026-10-16..22 by editor 'Geer of War', no stated source for numbers); community = forum / third-party guides; inferred = our reading, not stated anywhere
conventions.videoMining: 2026-10-23/24 sweep. YouTube watch pages via WebFetch return title only; r.jina.ai rendering gives description, chapters and a partial comment set but the transcript never loads ('NaN / NaN', 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot'); youtubetranscript.com reports YouTube is blocking subtitle fetches; yewtu.be API 403; reddit.com blocked. Numbers therefore come only from chapter titles and named commenters, labelled confidence 'video-transcribed' and NOT confirmed on screen. bonuses.name: Northern Migration
bonuses.text: Viking Villagers are not recruited normally; they are automatically recruited at no cost from Town Centers until the Villager capacity is reached. Longhouses increase the Villager capacity.

bonuses.name: Northern Migration (detail)
bonuses.text: Recruitment is at a slower rate than standard Villagers. Villager capacity +10 for each Longhouse constructed. Exact rate, base capacity and whether multiple TCs recruit in parallel are not stated.

bonuses.name: Living off the Land
bonuses.text: Infantry can heal themselves by gathering Food from deposits such as Berry Bushes, Deer or Boar. Official page: 'Any damage taken during raids can be healed by using Living of the Land on any Food source.' Heal rate unknown.

bonuses.name: Dock Influence
bonuses.text: Each Longhouse constructed within the influence of a Dock reduces the cost of all ships by 4%, up to a maximum of 16% (four Longhouses).

bonuses.name: Sagas
bonuses.text: Seven Sagas: quests completable at any time (raiding enemy buildings, hunting wild animals, trading, 'and more') that grant permanent economic or military bonuses; completed Sagas are commemorated by carved pillars near the Capital TC. Completion thresholds are not stated anywhere.

bonuses.name: Saga: Björn's Forage
bonuses.text: Infantry gain increased health and an improved charge.

bonuses.name: Saga: Falkr's Village
bonuses.text: Increases the speed Villagers are recruited and reduces the cost of Longhouse attachments.

bonuses.name: Saga: Hrafn's Raid
bonuses.text: Decreases the cost of technology and increases the speed of the Pasture & Loom and Smithy attachments.

bonuses.name: Saga: Jörmungandr's Trade
bonuses.text: Reduces the cost of Ships and Siege Weapons.

bonuses.name: Saga: Jofurr's Hunt
bonuses.text: Improves Villager gather speed and carry capacity.

bonuses.name: Saga: Ulfr's Forester
bonuses.text: Increases torch damage and attack range.

bonuses.name: Saga: Dreki's Temple
bonuses.text: Increases recruitment speed of Berserkers at Sacred Groves. Fandom: this Saga is unlocked by the Gullínn Temple landmark.

bonuses.name: Sacred Groves / Hamingja
bonuses.text: A Völur can be sacrificed to establish a Sacred Grove on a Relic. Groves periodically produce Berserkers and give the Hamingja buff to nearby units (fandom: increases armor of nearby units; the Grove regenerates HP when no enemies are near).

bonuses.name: Imperial population
bonuses.text: After reaching Imperial Age the Vikings can increase maximum population to 210 regardless of landmark; Folkekirken (via Kongens Dør Cathedral) raises it to 220.

bonuses.name: Late-game roster shift
bonuses.text: As the civilization develops it gains access to Knights (Jylland Knights, Castle Age) and 'Militia Crossbowmen' (fandom: Skâne Crossbowman).

bonuses.name: Starting conditions
bonuses.text: Not stated anywhere. Standard start (TC, Villagers, Scout, standard resources) is an assumption. Villager capacity at game start is unknown.

landmarks.name: Konungr Hall
landmarks.effect: Periodically provides Food and rallies Shield Maidens (official: Shield Maidens are recruited from the Konungr Hall landmark).

landmarks.name: Baugr Fort
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Barracks. Increases Barracks' work rate and reduces their technology costs. Immediately upgrades Bondi and Berserkers.

landmarks.name: Valdemar Castle
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Keep; grants the Danevirke Wall technology (all existing and new Palisades become Danevirke walls with much higher health and torch resistance). Increases the gold returned by Jylland Knights when killed.

landmarks.name: Gullínn Temple
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Sacred Grove. Allows Völur to establish Sacred Groves on Sacred Sites (not just Relics) and unlocks the Dreki's Temple Saga.

landmarks.name: Kongens Dør Cathedral
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Monastery. +10 population and maximum population. Periodically generates gold for each Longhouse within its slowly expanding aura. Unlocks Folkekirken (official).

landmarks.name: Ríkets Nyckel Castle
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Keep that fires volleys of arrows; recruits Skâne Crossbowmen on completion. +10 population and maximum population. Reduces the cost of all unit tier technologies.

uniqueUnits.name: Berserker
uniqueUnits.building: Barracks; also spawned by Sacred Grove
uniqueUnits.notes: Fast light melee infantry, dual axes, high damage. Berserkergang: at low health, heals and deals bonus damage for a time. Dark Age availability is fandom infobox only. Fandom S&W: strong vs light units, weak vs archers.

uniqueUnits.name: Bondi
uniqueUnits.notes: Replaces the Spearman. Higher health and armor, carries a shield; gains additional health / shield-wall ability when grouped.

uniqueUnits.name: Hirdman
uniqueUnits.age: unknown (Man-at-Arms replacement; standard MAA is Feudal)
uniqueUnits.notes: Replaces the Man-at-Arms: hard hitting, resilient, fast, 'comes with a higher cost'. Buffed by Ulfberht Swords.

uniqueUnits.name: Jylland Knight
uniqueUnits.notes: Cheaper replacement for Lancer/Knight with reduced damage and health; refunds part of its gold cost on death (Valdemar Castle increases the refund).

uniqueUnits.name: Skâne Crossbowman
uniqueUnits.building: unknown; also recruited on completion of Ríkets Nyckel Castle
uniqueUnits.age: unknown (officially 'Militia Crossbowmen' arrive as society develops)
uniqueUnits.notes: Cheaper Crossbowman replacement with reduced damage and health.

uniqueUnits.name: Shield Maiden
uniqueUnits.notes: Heavy ranged throwing-spear unit. Extra damage and movement speed near allied buildings; 'provide protection to Villagers'.

uniqueUnits.name: Völur
uniqueUnits.notes: Religious unit. Moves between Longhouses to boost production of their attachments, or is sacrificed to establish a Sacred Grove on a Relic (on Sacred Sites with Gullínn Temple).

uniqueUnits.name: Longship
uniqueUnits.notes: Archer ship that also transports units; each passenger adds health and one extra arrow. Extra Oars tech raises capacity and damage.

uniqueUnits.name: Drakkar
uniqueUnits.notes: Springald ship that throws nets to slow enemy ships; Snaerisspjot changes weapon to throwing spears (more range/damage).

uniqueUnits.name: Fishing Knarr
uniqueUnits.notes: Fishing Boat replacement that can also transport a small number of units.

uniqueBuildings.name: Longhouse
uniqueBuildings.effect: +10 Villager capacity, +25 maximum population. Can take ONE of four attachments. In-game description quoted by fandom: 'Increases your Villager capacity by +10 and your maximum Population by +25. Produces Bondi spearmen but 25% slower. Can be upgrade with one of four possible attachments'.

attachments.name: Bee Skeps
attachments.effect: Generates 50 gold per minute; +500 Longhouse HP

attachments.name: Farmstead
attachments.effect: Spawns two improved Farms; Longhouse becomes a Food drop-off; +500 Longhouse HP

attachments.name: Pasture and Loom
attachments.effect: Automatically researches melee and ranged armor technologies over time; +750 Longhouse HP

attachments.name: Smithy
attachments.effect: Automatically researches melee and ranged attack technologies over time; +750 Longhouse HP

uniqueBuildings.caveats: All numbers are from the fandom infobox/table created 2026-10-16..22 with no cited source; the infobox 'Use' line ('Drop off Food, Research Food-gathering improvements') looks copied from a Mill template and is not corroborated. Treat every number as provisional until the 17.0 extraction.

uniqueBuildings.name: Sacred Grove
uniqueBuildings.produces: Berserkers (periodic, free; rate unknown; Dreki's Temple Saga speeds it)
uniqueBuildings.effect: Established by sacrificing a Völur on a Relic (Sacred Sites with Gullínn Temple). Hamingja aura: increases armor of nearby units; regenerates HP when no enemies nearby.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Bondi Forester
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Each Bondi generates a passive trickle of wood.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Danevirke
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Palisade Walls become Danevirke Walls with increased HP and fire armor.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Extra Oars
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases Longship transport capacity and weapon damage.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Farmathr
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases Trader and Trade Ship health and movement speed.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Folkekirken
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases population and maximum population (official: to 220).

uniqueTechnologies.name: Hagl Brodda
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Archers fire two additional arrows at random when attacking.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Hamrammr
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Berserkergang triggers at a higher health threshold and heals additional HP.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Leding
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Dock influence bonus also increases ship production speed per Longhouse in influence.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Leikr Training
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases damage, health and range of melee infantry. Replaces Elite Army Tactics.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Reinforced Keel
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases health and ranged armor of all military ships.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Ship Barding
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases health and ranged armor of all military ships (fandom lists same text as Reinforced Keel; likely a tiered pair).

uniqueTechnologies.name: Snaerisspjot
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Drakkar weapon becomes throwing spears with increased range and damage.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Sunstones
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases ship movement speed and line of sight.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Turnshoes
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases melee infantry movement speed and charge damage.

economyNotes.text: Villagers are free and auto-recruited, gated by Villager capacity (+10 per Longhouse, 150 wood / 30 s each per fandom). This replaces the standard 50-food, 20-second TC queue entirely; the recruitment rate is 'slower than standard' and unpublished, so no villager-count curve can be computed yet.

Longhouse attachments give passive income: Bee Skeps 50 gold/min for 200 wood (limit 6 = up to 300 gold/min for 1,200 wood); Farmstead 200 wood for two improved farms plus a food drop-off (limit 6). Pasture & Loom / Smithy (100w+100g each, Feudal) auto-research Blacksmith armor/attack lines over time, replacing those gold costs. Völur boost attachment production.

Sagas with eco effects: Jofurr's Hunt (gather speed + carry), Falkr's Village (faster villager recruitment, cheaper attachments), Hrafn's Raid (cheaper tech, faster auto-research), Jörmungandr's Trade (cheaper ships/siege). Triggers are 'raiding enemy buildings, hunting wild animals, trading, and more' with no thresholds published.
Other trickles: Konungr Hall (Feudal landmark) periodically provides Food; Bondi Forester gives wood per Bondi; Kongens Dør Cathedral (Imperial) gives gold per Longhouse in aura. Amounts unknown.
Infantry heal by gathering food (Living off the Land) - raids can sustain without returning home.
Generic 17.0 change affecting all civs: Town Center construction time 150 -> 165 s. No general age-up cost changes listed in the 17.0 preview.
Age-up costs, landmark costs and starting resources are not published; standard values (400f/200g Feudal, 1200f/600g Castle, 2400f/1200g Imperial) would be an assumption.

openingsCommentary.summary: Official page 'Age 1': build an early Longhouse so Villager recruitment is never interrupted; upgrade Longhouses with Farmsteads or Bee Skeps for Food/Gold; early raids with Bondi and Berserkers, healing on food sources. 'Age 2': Pasture & Loom and Smithy 'usually good to buy early'; Völur to boost Longhouses or found a Sacred Grove on a Relic. 'Age 3': Valdemar Castle for Danevirke walls, Jylland Knights, Hagl Brodda. 'Age 4': pop 210/220, Leikr Training.
Steam / 17.0 notes framing: early raiding with fast melee infantry and 'early naval dominance'; 'every successful strike against an enemy economy fuels your own' (Sagas).

Community pre-release guide (aoeinfo.net, updated 2026-10-10): explicitly states no costs, stats or build order exist yet; plans to track villager split, Feudal timing, first-raid timing after release.
Official forum thread (58 posts, Jun-Oct 2026) contains only reactions and speculation (e.g., Longhouse attachment screenshots showing vegetables/honey/meat variants); no stats or openings.
